speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin the assessment of your neck swelling, could you describe the location of the mass and how long it has been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the mass feel soft and doughy, and is it easily compressible? Also, have you noticed any changes in your weight, skin color, or hair growth recently?

The ultrasound findings will help distinguish between a lipoma, cyst, or lymphadenopathy, especially given your history of colon cancer.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound suggests a cystic lesion, so I need to determine if it is connected to deeper structures. Is the mass fluctuant, and does it transilluminate when a light is shone through it?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Colon cancer (colectomy performed), type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, osteoarthritis of the left knee. Social history: Works as a traffic warden, frequently plays golf.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, I must rule out metastasis despite the cystic appearance. Has the mass changed in size rapidly, or have you experienced any night sweats or unexplained weight loss?

speaker: Patient

REQUEST TEST: Fine_Needle_Aspiration_Cytology
Given the cystic nature on ultrasound and your history of colon cancer, cytology is essential to rule out metastatic disease or an epidermoid cyst.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the cytology is normal and the lesion is cystic, it is likely a benign epidermoid cyst. Does the mass have a central punctum or pore on its surface, and has it ever drained thick, cheesy material?

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the normal cytology, the cystic nature and location on the nape of the neck are highly characteristic of a pilonidal cyst. I will request medical images to visually confirm the presence of a sinus tract or punctum. REQUEST IMAGES
